title: CountNonZero primitive ignores documented dims constructor argument and fails on CPU
duplicate_search_queries: site:gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/issues CountNonZero dims inputs number should be 2 got 1 MindSpore
site:github.com/mindspore-ai/mindspore/issues CountNonZero dims inputs number should be 2 got 1 MindSpore
duplicate_search_result: No exact matching GitHub or Gitee issue found for CountNonZero constructor dims failing with one documented input.
documentation_notes: MindSpore 2.9 local help(ops.CountNonZero) shows signature CountNonZero(dims=None), documents dims as Union[int, tuple(int), list(int)], lists CPU support, and includes the example ops.CountNonZero(dims=[1])(x).
The installed 2.9 operations/array_ops.py source has CountNonZero.__init__(self, dims=None), init_prim_io_names(inputs=['x'], outputs=['y']), and adds dims as a primitive attribute.
The installed 2.9 auto_generate/gen_ops_prim.py source defines another CountNonZero with __call__(self, input, dim=None), which expects a call-time dim input.
The public functional ops.count_nonzero documents axis as Union[int, tuple(int), list(int)] and CPU support, and the functional axis-list control passes in both execution modes.
classification_notes: Not a numerical precision issue: the primitive raises before producing a tensor.
Not a bad input issue: the failing form is copied from the local public CountNonZero docstring shape, and the same axis list passes through ops.count_nonzero on CPU.
Not localized to one execution mode: both PyNative and Graph mode fail, with different symptoms caused by the constructor dims not being wired into the active primitive call path.
The PyNative error says CountNonZero expects 2 inputs but got 1. The Graph error lowers dim as None and then reports CountNonZero unsupported on CPU.
